source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Community health nursing is broader than public health nursing because it also includes:
questions.rationale: CHN includes public health nursing, occupational health nursing and school nursing; hospital nursing is the other major field.
explanations: Not in the CHN scope described.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Community health nursing (PDF p. 17)
questions.quote: it includes public health nursing, occupational health nursing and school nursing.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: In community health nursing, who is considered the primary client?
questions.rationale: CHN clients are individuals, families, population groups and the community, with the community as the primary client.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Clients of CHN (PDF p. 18)
questions.quote: There are different levels of clientele in community health nursing—the individual, family, population group and community, with the latter as the primary client.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes community health nursing practice?
options: It focuses mainly on curing illness
The nurse makes decisions for clients
It deals only with sick individuals
questions.rationale: CHN is comprehensive, general and continual, aims at health promotion and disease prevention, and nurse and client collaborate as equals.
explanations: Promotion and prevention are the goals.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Community health nursing (PDF p. 17)
questions.quote: Community health nursing practice is comprehensive, general, continual and not episodic

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Population Groups
questions.stem: Pregnant women in a barangay who share common health needs and risks are best described as a:
questions.rationale: A population group shares characteristics, developmental stage or exposures and therefore common health problems.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Population group (PDF p. 19)
questions.quote: A population group is a group of people who share common characteristics, developmental stage or common exposure to particular environmental factors

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: In the community-as-partner model, what lies at the core of the assessment wheel?
questions.rationale: The core is the people (demographics, values, beliefs, history), surrounded by eight subsystems.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Community (PDF p. 20)
questions.quote: At the core of the assessment wheel are the people of the community—their demographics, values, beliefs and history.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: The three core functions of public health are assessment, policy development and:
questions.rationale: Assurance means making sure health services are effective, available and accessible.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Public health (PDF p. 23)
questions.quote: Today public health could be defined in terms of its three core functions: assessment, policy development and assurance.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: The PHN regularly collects and analyzes barangay health data to guide program planning. This public health core function is:
questions.rationale: Assessment is the regular collection and analysis of health data for planning and policy.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Public health (PDF p. 23)
questions.quote: Assessment is the regular collection and analysis of health data.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: "The science and art of preventing disease, prolonging life, and promoting health and efficiency through organized community effort" is the definition of public health by:
questions.rationale: This is Winslow's (1920) classic definition of public health.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Public health (PDF p. 23)
questions.quote: One of the most quoted definitions of public health is that of Winslow (1920)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Under the Local Government Code (RA 7160), the rural health units and barangay health stations were devolved to the:
questions.rationale: In 1993, RHUs and BHSs went to municipal governments; provincial and district hospitals went to provinces.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Devolution (PDF p. 26)
questions.quote: the provincial governments and the rural health units (RHUs) and barangay health stations (BHSs) to the municipal governments.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Who chairs the Municipal Health Board?
questions.rationale: At city and municipal level the mayor chairs the Local Health Board; the municipal health officer is vice chair.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Devolution (PDF p. 26)
questions.quote: At the city and municipal level, the LHB is composed of the following: mayor (chair), municipal health officer (vice chair)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A main function of the Local Health Board is to:
questions.rationale: The LHB proposes budgetary allocations for local health facilities and services.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Devolution (PDF p. 26)
questions.quote: It is mandated to propose annual budgetary allocations for the operation and maintenance of health facilities and services

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A town's crude birth rate is 22 per 1,000 and crude death rate is 6 per 1,000. The rate of natural increase is:
questions.rationale: Rate of natural increase = CBR − CDR = 22 − 6 = 16 per 1,000 population.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Births and deaths (PDF p. 28)
questions.quote: the rate of natural increase in the country's population for the same year was 18.3 (23.1 minus 4.8) for every 1000 population

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: According to the WHO, a woman's death counts as a maternal death if it occurs during pregnancy or within how many days after the end of pregnancy?
questions.rationale: Maternal death: during pregnancy or within 42 days of its termination, from causes related to or aggravated by pregnancy, not accidental causes.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Maternal mortality (PDF p. 29)
questions.quote: the death ofa woman while pregnant or within 42 days of termination of pregnancy

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A pregnant woman dies in a road accident. For vital statistics, this is:
questions.rationale: Maternal deaths exclude accidental or incidental causes.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Maternal mortality (PDF p. 29)
questions.quote: but not from accidental or incidental causes.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Primary health care was adopted as the approach to "Health for All" at the 1978 conference held in:
questions.rationale: The Declaration on Primary Health Care was signed at Alma-Ata, USSR, in 1978.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Primary health care (PDF p. 31)
questions.quote: In 1978, representatives from 134 countries who attended the International Conference on Primary Health Care in Alma-Ata, USSR signed the Declaration

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Primary health care is essential health care made accessible to families "at a cost the community can afford," in the spirit of:
questions.rationale: PHC stresses full community participation, affordability, self-reliance and self-determination.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Primary health care (PDF p. 32)
questions.quote: in the spirit of self reliance and self determination

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which is one of the essential elements of primary health care?
options: Provision of safe water and sanitation
questions.rationale: PHC elements include health education, nutrition, immunization, safe water and sanitation, MCH and FP, endemic disease control, treatment of common diseases and essential drugs.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Primary health care (PDF p. 32)
questions.quote: provision of safe water and basic sanitation

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A PHN works with the DepEd, DSWD and an NGO to address child malnutrition in a town. This PHC strategy is:
questions.rationale: Because health problems are multi-causal, the CHN works with other sectors and NGOs (intersectoral linkage).
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Primary health care (PDF p. 32)
questions.quote: Multisectoral linkage ensures that the different facets of health problems are addressed.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Health Education
questions.stem: The Ottawa Charter (1986) defines health promotion as:
questions.rationale: Health promotion is the process of enabling people to increase control over, and to improve, their health.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Health promotion (PDF p. 33)
questions.quote: The Charter defines health promotion as "the process of enabling people to increase control over, and to improve, their health".

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Health Education
questions.stem: Which is one of the five action areas of the Ottawa Charter?
questions.rationale: The five areas: healthy public policy, supportive environments, community action, personal skills, and reorienting health services.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Health promotion (PDF p. 33)
questions.quote: building healthy public policy, creating supportive environments, strengthening community action, developing personal skills and reorienting health services

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A PHN actively looks for undiagnosed TB cases in a squatter area. This population-oriented role is:
questions.rationale: Clark groups CHN roles as client-oriented, delivery-oriented and population-oriented; case finding is population-oriented.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Roles of CHNs (PDF p. 18)
questions.quote: population- oriented roles (case finder, leader, change agent, community mobilizer, coalition builder, policy advocate, social marketer and researcher).

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: In evaluating an immunization program, the vaccines and syringes are considered the program's:
questions.rationale: Inputs are essential resources; outputs are services produced; effects result from outputs; impact is the long-range outcome.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Evaluation (PDF p. 37)
questions.quote: Inputs are the important resources the program cannot do without (e.g., Iron and Vitamin A for a nutrition program and vaccines for an immunization program).

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A decrease in infant deaths in the municipality after 5 years of the immunization program reflects the program's:
questions.rationale: Impact is the broad, long-range result of program effects.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Evaluation (PDF p. 38)
questions.quote: Impact is the outcome of program effects and is an expression of broader, long-range program objectives

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Integrated: Professional Practice, Ethics & Law
questions.stem: A PHN says, "Documentation is just extra work." Which reason best supports careful documentation?
questions.rationale: Documentation proves nursing judgment, protects against lawsuits, shows workload and supports research and QA.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Documentation (PDF p. 38)
questions.quote: it is generally believed that what is not written was not done

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Integrated: Professional Practice, Ethics & Law
questions.stem: When advocating for a vulnerable community before the municipal council, the nurse should:
questions.rationale: Advocacy articulates clients' perspectives while respecting their autonomy, until they can speak for themselves.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Advocacy (PDF p. 40)
questions.quote: in doing advocacy, they uphold a client's autonomy, which means that they reserve for their clients the right to make their own decisions.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Integrated: Professional Practice, Ethics & Law
questions.stem: The health center has only one dose of an expensive medicine left and two patients with the same need. Following the equity rule, the PHN gives it to:
options: The patient less able to pay
questions.rationale: Distributive justice and the equity rule: scarce resources go to the one in greater need, including inability to pay.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Ethicolegal aspects (PDF p. 45)
questions.quote: the scarce resources should be given to the one who is in greater need. "Need" is dictated not only by one's health condition but also by his inability to pay.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Integrated: Professional Practice, Ethics & Law
questions.stem: A mother refuses the IUD offered at the health center. The PHN should:
options: Continue giving her other health services
questions.rationale: Clients' refusal of a specific FP method should not affect their access to other health services.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 Ethicolegal aspects (PDF p. 45)
questions.quote: Clients' refusal (e.g., specific FP methods) should not affect their access to other health services.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Population Groups
questions.stem: Most activities of school nurses focus on health promotion and disease prevention because:
questions.rationale: School children (like workers) are generally well, so school nursing centers on promotion, prevention and early detection.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 School nursing (PDF p. 44)
questions.quote: school children who are in school are generally well. For this reason, most of the activities of school nurses are focused on health advocacy, health promotion, disease prevention

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: In the absence of the rural health physician, who manages the rural health unit?
questions.rationale: Among the PHN's management functions is managing the RHU when the rural health physician is absent.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 PHN functions (PDF p. 41)
questions.quote: Manages the RHU in the absence of the rural health physician (RHP).

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: The PHN reviews the barangay health plans of the midwives and guides them in corrective measures. This function is:
questions.rationale: The PHN supervises rural health midwives, including technical supervision of barangay health plans.
questions.source: Maglaya, Nursing Practice in the Community, 5th ed. (2009), Ch. 1 PHN functions (PDF p. 42)
questions.quote: Guides the midwives in the formulation of barangay health plans
